title: Drugs that lower the seizure threshold
scopeNotes: Labels and an FDA safety communication; Beers 2023 items apply to adults ≥65

entries.title: Bupropion
effect: Dose-related seizures: ~0.4% at up to 450 mg/day (IR label)
pearls: Contraindicated: seizure disorder; current or prior bulimia/anorexia; abrupt withdrawal of alcohol, benzodiazepines, barbiturates or antiseizure medications
Other risk factors (label): severe head injury, AVM, CNS tumor or infection, severe stroke, metabolic disorders (hypoglycemia, hyponatremia, hypoxia), other threshold-lowering drugs
IR: max 450 mg/day, ≤150 mg per dose, titrate gradually; stop if a seizure occurs
SR and XL maximum doses differ from IR — not covered by the label on file
sources: Bupropion hydrochloride tablets US prescribing information. Cipla; revised 3/2023 (user-supplied label)

entries.title: Flumazenil
effect: Seizures, most often after long-term benzodiazepine sedation or in overdose with serious cyclic antidepressant toxicity
pearls: Contraindicated when a benzodiazepine is controlling a life-threatening condition (e.g., ICP, status epilepticus) or with signs of serious cyclic antidepressant overdose
Precipitates withdrawal seizures in benzodiazepine-dependent patients
Not recommended to diagnose benzodiazepine sedation in the ICU
Watch for resedation after reversal
sources: Flumazenil injection US prescribing information. Akorn-Strides; revised 5/2008 (user-supplied label)

entries.title: Cefepime
effect: Non-convulsive status epilepticus — FDA review: 59 cases, nearly all with renal impairment; 56 without renal dose adjustment
pearls: Mean onset ~6 days (range 1–15) in published cases; most recover after stopping cefepime ± antiseizure treatment
Unexplained confusion on cefepime, especially older or renally impaired: consider EEG
Dose to renal function per label and reassess as renal function changes
sources: FDA Drug Safety Communication on cefepime and non-convulsive status epilepticus (2012), as summarized in: Song JC. Cefepime: FDA Drug Safety Communication on non-convulsive status epilepticus risk. Infect Dis Alert 2012;31(11)

entries.title: Other beta-lactams and carbapenems
effect: Non-convulsive status epilepticus reported, including 8 published ceftazidime cases (onset 3–8 days, nearly all with renal impairment)
pearls: Risk factors for antibiotic-induced seizures: prior seizures, renal impairment, meningitis/CNS infection, extremes of age, low albumin
Carbapenems also lower valproate levels — see asm-interactions
sources: FDA Drug Safety Communication on cefepime and non-convulsive status epilepticus (2012), as summarized in: Song JC. Cefepime: FDA Drug Safety Communication on non-convulsive status epilepticus risk. Infect Dis Alert 2012;31(11)

entries.title: Fluoroquinolones
effect: Non-convulsive status epilepticus reported; ciprofloxacin raises CNS risk (seizures, confusion) when CrCl <30
pearls: Beers 2023 (adults ≥65): ciprofloxacin doses usually need reduction at CrCl <30 mL/min
Also on the MG caution list
sources: FDA Drug Safety Communication on cefepime and non-convulsive status epilepticus (2012), as summarized in: Song JC. Cefepime: FDA Drug Safety Communication on non-convulsive status epilepticus risk. Infect Dis Alert 2012;31(11)

entries.title: Theophylline
effect: Seizures with toxicity (often >30 mcg/mL); isolated seizures reported below 20 mcg/mL in older patients and those with neurologic disease
pearls: Label: extreme caution in seizure disorders
Toxicity seizures are hard to stop — benzodiazepines then phenobarbital; label calls for rapid, aggressive treatment
Ciprofloxacin raises theophylline levels — avoid the combination (Beers 2023)
Many conditions and drugs reduce clearance; label advises frequent serum concentrations in acutely ill patients
sources: Theophylline anhydrous extended-release tablets US prescribing information. Westminster; revised 12/2025 (user-supplied label)

entries.title: Clozapine
effect: Dose-related seizures: ~5% cumulative incidence at 1 year
pearls: Boxed warning includes seizure
Start 12.5 mg, titrate slowly, divided doses
Caution with prior seizures or risk factors (head trauma, CNS pathology, threshold-lowering drugs, alcohol use)
Counsel against driving, swimming or climbing
sources: Clozapine tablets US prescribing information. Accord; revised 10/2025 (user-supplied label)

entries.title: Tramadol
effect: Seizures within the recommended dose range; risk rises above it
pearls: Higher risk with epilepsy or prior seizures, head trauma, metabolic disorders, alcohol/drug withdrawal, CNS infection
Risk rises with SSRIs, TCAs and tricyclic compounds (e.g., cyclobenzaprine), other opioids, MAOIs, neuroleptics
With carbamazepine: not recommended — less analgesia and added seizure risk
In overdose, naloxone may increase seizure risk
Beers 2023 (≥65): reduce IR dose and avoid ER at CrCl <30
Label on file is the 2010 Ultram ER label
sources: Ultram ER (tramadol HCl) extended-release tablets US prescribing information (Rebel Distributors); revised 12/2010 (user-supplied label)

entries.title: Meperidine
effect: Seizures with or without a seizure disorder; prolonged use and renal impairment accumulate the neurotoxic metabolite normeperidine
pearls: Label: monitor seizure control in patients with epilepsy; titrate slowly and watch for CNS toxicity in renal impairment
Contraindicated with MAOIs or within 14 days of stopping one
Beers 2023 (≥65): avoid — neurotoxicity including delirium; safer alternatives exist
sources: Demerol (meperidine hydrochloride) injection US prescribing information. Hospira; revised 12/2025 (user-supplied label)
